topics.label: Introduction and lecture objectives
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic frames the lecture's subject and objectives before the substantive discussion begins.

topics.label: Cancer as clonal evolution
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains cancer development through clonal evolution within a permissive microenvironment.

topics.label: Intrinsic and environmental contributions to cancer risk
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine the evidence and debate about how different sources of cancer risk contribute to disease.

topics.label: Infection-driven cancer development
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how infectious agents contribute to cancer, with Burkitt lymphoma providing a specific example.

topics.label: Carcinogen-induced DNA damage
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics trace how carcinogenic exposures produce DNA damage through direct or indirect mechanisms.

topics.label: Tumour initiation, promotion and tissue susceptibility
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain how carcinogenic effects depend on tumour promotion and tissue susceptibility, ending with a summary of the preceding mechanisms.

topics.label: Human evidence of carcinogen exposure and carcinogenicity
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics show how measurable evidence in humans supports the identification and assessment of carcinogenic exposures.

topics.label: Experimental carcinogenicity testing and its limitations
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics examine experimental tests used to assess carcinogenic potential and the limitations of interpreting their results.

topics.label: Lecture summary and risk–benefit decisions
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic closes the lecture by reviewing its main conclusions about environmental cancer risks and their assessment.
